reasoning_summary: The configuration is sound. Re is 100, the inlet is uniform (ux_nonuniformity 0.0), blockage is 0.0125, the upstream distance is 30 D, mass imbalance is 8.3333e-11, and max Courant is 0.73373. The problem is how the quantities were sampled and how well they are resolved.

Drag statistics are too weak for a 3 % tolerance. The stationary window has only 3 cycles. The mean drag 95 % CI is 0.044509, which is about 3.4 % of 1.3039 and already above 3 %. Relative drift of mean drag is 0.040105, which is above 3 %. The half-window difference is null, so stationarity of the mean was not demonstrated.

The declared averaging start (10 convective units) is before the detected end of the transient (15.276). The submitted-setup mean drag (1.2961) therefore includes transient data. It differs from the stationary-window value (1.3039), so the result depends on window choice.

Strouhal frequency resolution is 0.033333, about 20 % of St (about 0.16). The 3 % tolerance is about 0.005. The three estimates (0.16129, 0.16058, 0.16169) agree within about 1 %, but with only 3 cycles and this resolution the 3 % claim is not supported by the spectral evidence.

Spatial resolution is modest and was not checked. The mesh has 30580 cells, a representative cell size of 0.45745 D, a last wake cell of 1.0209 D, and max non-orthogonality of 43.313 deg. Only one run exists, so there is no mesh or time-step sensitivity evidence.

Overall, the statistical uncertainty on mean drag already exceeds the requested tolerance, and Strouhal is under-resolved with a short record. I do not consider the two quantities trustworthy to 3 % from this evidence.
